findings.text: The node's follow-on (1) recommends REMOVING the membership guard at 11540-11541 because 'classify_parked_source is total, so no input makes it fire'. The observation is correct and the recommendation is reversed. TRIGGERING INPUT: add a seventh branch to classify_parked_source returning a string the frozenset does not name - e.g. `if str(evidence.get("lifecycle_status") or "").strip() == "deprecated": return "upstream_quantity_deprecated"` - then call record_parked_dispositions([{ "id": "sns-1", "lifecycle_status": "deprecated" }]). With the guard present it raises ValueError before any write. With the guard removed as the follow-on recommends, BOTH new tests are still green: no BRANCH_CASES entry supplies lifecycle_status 'deprecated', so test_every_branch_returns_a_declared_disposition never evaluates the new branch, and test_the_representative_inputs_cover_the_whole_declared_set still finds reached == the declared set because the six given inputs are unchanged. The undeclared string is then written to the graph: written.append({"id": row["id"], "disposition": disposition}) at 11542 is unconditional and _CAP_DISPOSITION_WRITE at 11544 is called whenever written is non-empty, so the row lands carrying a disposition the census at 11668 does not name. The guard's aperture is every row; the new test's aperture is six representative inputs. The guard is the only runtime tripwire for the drift the test cannot reach, and it is dead TODAY only because the classifier has no seventh branch today. Keep it. The delivered tree is correct as it stands - this finding is an instruction not to action the follow-on, not a defect in what landed. VERDICT: MUST-NOT-ACTION: the follow-on as written would remove a live runtime protection while the suite stays green.

The node's follow-on (2) is true as an observation and has zero marginal effect, and it misattributes the guard's purpose. The guard's own module docstring at 11531-11533 states what it refuses: 'A classification outside CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS refuses before any write, so no caller can end with a row carrying an unclassified disposition'. Its subject is an unclassified DISPOSITION, not a malformed row. The subscript `row['id']` inside the f-string at 11541 is real, but the row it would KeyError on also subscripts `row["id"]` unconditionally at 11542 - one line later, from the same row - so the failure class is KeyError either way and the proposed `row.get("id")` changes nothing an operator could observe. TRIGGERING INPUT for the KeyError: record_parked_dispositions([{ "last_error": "compose request timed out" }]) raises KeyError: 'id' at 11542 today (the guard at 11540 does not fire, since the classifier returns a declared member). The row shape is unreachable from the only caller's own query, __CAP_PARKED_QUERY at 11507-11517, which always projects `sns.id AS id`. Cosmetic at most; the guard cannot fire, so the f-string cannot be the thing that raises. VERDICT: NIT, and the premise ('the one malformed row the guard exists to describe') is not what the guard describes.

The delivered tests pin vocabulary membership and member reachability, but not the classifier's PRECEDENCE, so 'each branch reached exactly once' is measured rather than asserted. TRIGGERING INPUT: invert the order of the last two conditions in classify_parked_source so the node_category test precedes the last_error test, then call classify_parked_source({"last_error": "compose request timed out", "node_category": "geometry"}). Both tests still pass, because no BRANCH_CASES entry supplies two simultaneous conditions, yet that input moves from attempt_budget_exhausted to compose_not_applicable and the census counts change. This is an aperture limit of a six-case table rather than a defect - the precedence is documented in the docstring at 11444-11445 ('A recorded cause outranks the node category') and the new tests do not contradict it - so this is a note for whoever widens the table, not a MUST-FIX. Blast radius is a census reclassification, never a wrong write: the classifier cannot return an undeclared value while the table and set agree.

justifications.durability: The delivered shape is the durable one and it is the right shape: the tests pin the CONTRACT (return value is a declared member) rather than a snapshot of the classifier, so they hold as the implementation is refactored, and adding a member to CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS fails test 2 until a representative input actually reaches it - a ratchet in the correct direction. Two residuals, one of which matters. READ FIRST the finding on graph_ops.py:11540: this node's follow-on (1) tells the coordinator to delete the membership guard, and that instruction is wrong in a way that survives this node's own suite. The durability question for a follow-on is whether actioning it keeps the protection, and here it does not: the tests cover six representative inputs while the guard covers every row, so removing the guard loses the only tripwire against an undeclared disposition returned for an unrepresented input, and the write at 11544 would carry it to the graph. A hand-off that would silently remove a protection is a durability cost of this node even though the delivered tree is correct, which is why this dimension is 16 rather than 19. SECOND, the delivered tests do not pin the classifier's precedence (see the third finding): a six-case table fixes the branch set, not the order in which conditions are tested, so a reordering that reclassifies a doubly-qualifying row is green across both tests. That is an aperture limit, not a defect, and it is the same reason the guard earns its place.
justifications.evidence: Strong for a test-addition node, and I reproduced the load-bearing measurement rather than reading it off the manifest. The zero-added claim is real: I extracted the FAILED/ERROR id set from baseline_sn.log and after_sn.log myself and diffed them - byte-identical, 23 ids each, zero added and zero removed, with pytest's own totals corroborating (baseline '20 failed, 7536 passed, 8 skipped, 3 errors'; after '20 failed, 7538 passed, 8 skipped, 3 errors'). The delta between the two runs is exactly the node's two new tests: collected rose 7893 to 7895 and passed rose 7536 to 7538 with the failure set unmoved, which is the cleanest possible attribution - the node's tests both passed in after_sn.log at the 63% progress marker (the short summary reads 'test_parked_disposition_vocabulary.py ..'), so both new tests are green in the same run whose failure set the node did not move. THE TWO-TREE LABEL IS CORRECT, which is the one thing this review was asked to adjudicate, and I verified it by mechanism rather than by the worker's say-so. after_suite_mainenv.log was produced by `uv run --directory /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex pytest <worktree>/tests/standard_names/`, so both the project and the CWD resolved to the MAIN checkout while the collected tests came from the worktree - and the log itself proves the pairing rather than merely permitting it: its short-summary lines print the test paths RELATIVE to main's CWD ('../.reckon-worktrees/imas-codex-c994bf55fb01/ship-s10-20260918/n-the-parked-disposition-vocabulary-is-pinned/tests/standard_names/test_export_deprecation.py'), which is main as the working directory and the worktree as the test source in one line. The import side is pinned by the tree layout: tests/standard_names/__init__.py EXISTS and tests/__init__.py does NOT, so pytest's prepend import mode inserts <tree>/tests - never the tree root - on sys.path, meaning `import imas_codex` could not have been served by the worktree and fell to main's editable install. The collected count agrees: the mainenv run collected the SAME 7895 tests as the single-tree run, which identifies the collected set as the worktree's tests rather than main's, so the only variable between the two runs is which SOURCE TREE served the import. Two trees, exactly as labelled, and correctly excluded from the gate. It also corroborates the concurrent node's ownership of the surplus - mainenv minus after_sn is exactly 23 ids, distributed 16 test_review_release.py / 2 test_review_release_preview_link.py / 2 test_review_body_authored.py / 2 test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py / 1 test_review_release_checkout.py, every one of them in the concurrent release-fixture node's files and NONE in this node's file. And to be explicit about the risk the question raises: even had the label been wrong, the zero-added claim does not rest on that run at all - it rests on baseline_sn.log and after_sn.log, both single-tree (PYTHONPATH=$PWD with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT pointing at the shared .venv, the repository's documented worktree recipe), and that pair I diffed myself. The negative control is the right mutation for this property: a scratch copy of classify_parked_source outside the repository returns 'grammar_gap_not_declared' instead of 'grammar_gap' - recorded verbatim on its first line - so it breaks exactly the classifier-and-frozenset agreement the tests exist to hold, and BOTH tests go red (2 failed in 5.47s), which is correct since an undeclared return breaks totality and coverage together. One reservation on aperture rather than rigour: the mutation was applied to a scratch copy rather than by reverting in-tree, so it demonstrates the assertions without a single-tree revert; for a pure-function pin that is adequate and avoids contaminating the tree, and the red log is genuinely a red log. I also confirmed the node trips nothing else: the 23 pre-existing standard-names failures are identical before and after, all in the export/reconcile surface, and none is in this node's file.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this repository and for a pure-function pin. The module opens with a docstring that states the MECHANISM (totality holds because the two definitions agree, not because anything enforces it) and the concrete drift it prevents ('a seventh branch, or a renamed disposition string, would leave the classifier returning a value the frozenset does not name and nothing would say so') rather than narrating a changelog. Tests need no fixtures and no graph, so they run in the default tier in 5.47s (negative_control_red.log), which is the right cost for a property this cheap to check. BRANCH_CASES carries a comment naming the classifier's own precedence as the ordering key, and test 2 copies each case with dict(evidence) rather than mutating the module-level table. Naming is by what the file tests - test_parked_disposition_vocabulary.py - with no plan label, sprint id, ticket reference or author attribution in the filename, symbols, comments or docstrings; BRANCH_CASES, CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS and the two test names all read without plan context. All four commits carry a conventional subject and a substantive body, and I ran the trailer check on each: c13646f62, 969d03e82, 04edfc74a, bf77bfcca all clean, no AI attribution, no plan or ticket identifiers. The evidence archive gains an inline SVG branch-to-set diagram with the mutation member drawn dashed in the refusal colour (id="bmut"), which is the repository's figures-in-evidence convention. The one thing a reader may over-read is the module docstring's closing claim that the pair 'fails the moment the function and the frozenset drift apart instead of never' - true for the six represented inputs, and the reason the guard at 11540 should stay.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The brief was to pin the six declared members of the parked-disposition vocabulary so that each branch of the classifier is reached exactly once. The node delivered exactly that. Verified against the source rather than the report: CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS at graph_ops.py:11405 declares six members (name_produced, upstream_quantity_removed, compose_not_applicable, vocabulary_gap, attempt_budget_exhausted, cause_not_recorded), and classify_parked_source at 11431-11458 has six return sites, each a literal drawn from that set, with the fallthrough at 11458 returning cause_not_recorded. BRANCH_CASES supplies one input per site: produced=1 for the produced guard; lifecycle_status='removed'; last_error containing the lexical marker 'vocabulary gap'; last_error='compose request timed out', which is genuinely distinct from _COMPOSE_CAP_REASON at 11399 ('compose claim-attempt cap reached') and so reaches attempt_budget_exhausted rather than falling through; node_category='geometry' for the category guard; and an empty dict for the silence case. Test 2 passing is the machine-checked proof that this mapping is one-to-one onto the declared set - reached == set(CAP_PARKED_DISPOSITIONS) - so no member is dead and no branch is missed. Executed at the integrated head: the 2 tests pass both in the single-tree run (after_sn.log: '..' at 63%) and in the mixed-tree run. Full SHAs verified: the commit is c13646f626db9eab93037fbf509e194a7a4ccc08, reachable from main (merge-base --is-ancestor at main HEAD f2cb7b21b), and the classifier text at 11431 on main is the text the tests exercise. The reason this is 19 rather than 20 is the precedence aperture described in the third finding: the table pins which branches exist, not the order in which the classifier tests them, so a reordering that reclassifies a doubly-qualifying row passes both tests.
justifications.scope_discipline: Clean on every axis I checked. The whole diff d6dbd2a0e..bf77bfcca is 2 files and 213 insertions with ZERO deletions: tests/standard_names/test_parked_disposition_vocabulary.py (59 lines, all added) and docs/evidence/archive/sn-lifecycle-integrity-landed.html (154 lines, all added). No production file changed - imas_codex/ is untouched by the node, which matters because the two follow-ons it reports are edits it deliberately did NOT make. No conftest, no shared fixture, no existing test modified, no assertion weakened anywhere. The plan file is handled correctly and the handling is worth recording: docs/plans/sn-lifecycle-integrity.html is net-zero against base (git diff --stat d6dbd2a0e..bf77bfcca over that path prints for zero files for zero lines), so the node landed a local plan comment at 969d03e82 and then withdrew it at 04edfc74a once the coordinator reported the plan had moved on main, rather than forcing its edit against the coordinator's move. It left the plan advance to the coordinator and said so in the manifest under PLAN_WRITE_DROPPED, which is the correct behaviour when the plan is the coordinator's to write. Nothing was pushed or merged by the worker (main's HEAD f2cb7b21b is a coordinator merge), no branch was created, and no out-of-scope path was staged. All four commits carry conventional subjects with bodies; the trailer check is clean on each; no plan label, sprint id, stage name or ticket number appears in a subject, a symbol, a filename or a comment.
